items.stem: A factory could produce either tables or chairs with the same wood and hours. The cost of making tables, expressed economically, is best described as:

options.text: The chairs given up to make the tables (opportunity cost)
options.rationale: Correct: opportunity cost is the value of the next-best forgone option.

options.text: Only the money spent on wood
options.rationale: That ignores the forgone alternative, which is the economic cost.

options.text: Zero, because the wood was already owned
options.rationale: Owning the input does not eliminate opportunity cost.
Revenue is not the cost of the choice.

items.explanation: Correct: opportunity cost is the value of the next-best forgone option.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which statements about supply and demand are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: A fall in consumer income can shift the demand curve
options.rationale: Correct: income is a determinant that shifts demand, not a movement along it.

options.text: A change in the good's own price causes a movement along the curve
options.rationale: Correct: price changes move along the curve rather than shifting it.

options.text: A change in price shifts the entire demand curve
options.rationale: A price change is a movement along the curve, not a shift.

options.text: Supply and demand never affect market price
options.rationale: Their interaction is precisely what sets market price.

items.explanation: Correct: income is a determinant that shifts demand, not a movement along it.

items.stem: A pollution cost borne by a nearby community but not paid by the factory is an example of:

options.rationale: Correct: a cost imposed on third parties outside the market transaction.
Externalities are a form of market failure, not efficiency.

options.text: An opportunity cost to the factory
options.rationale: The cost falls on others, not as a forgone option for the firm.
Inflation is a general rise in prices, unrelated here.

items.explanation: Correct: a cost imposed on third parties outside the market transaction.
